program: Community mental health, family support, residential care, housing and mobile crisis response

acceptance.evidence: docs/la-next-four-acceptance.md — independent primary-source, financial and model audit plus root scope acceptance.

what: Sycamores combines community mental-health treatment with residential care, housing, school support and mobile crisis response.
The estimate uses its large community/clinic program as a clinical component while charging the entire recipient's resources.
Its teams work with young people and families across clinics, schools, homes and crisis settings.
strengths: The organization participated in relevant randomized modular youth-therapy research.
Current services include sustained clinical care, not just crisis contacts or awareness.
Original returns identify a substantial clinical budget and allow gross-cost reconciliation.
reservations: The cost per compatible treatment course and response to new funding are subjective assumptions.
The QALY bridge comes from children with epilepsy in the UK, not an observed Sycamores health effect.
Housing, residential, crisis and training benefits remain unpriced; the component price is not a portfolio ranking.

sections.what:
This report covers the whole Hathaway-Sycamores Child and Family Services recipient, EIN 95-1691005. Its [current portfolio](https://www.sycamores.org/services/) includes outpatient and intensive family treatment, residential care, school services, housing, mobile crisis response and professional training. The [behavioral-health page](https://www.sycamores.org/behavioral-health/) describes integrated therapy, medication support, substance-use care and wraparound services.

The [crisis program](https://www.sycamores.org/mobile-crisis-outreach-team/) operates in both LA and Riverside Counties; CIRCLE handles non-urgent calls concerning unhoused people in the San Fernando Valley. Neither every crisis response nor every person reached is a suicide averted. The modeled LA/Orange share of the clinical component is 90%, an explicit residence judgment rather than headquarters attribution.
sections.monitoring:
The [homepage](https://www.sycamores.org/) reports reaching over 37,000 children, youth and families. That broad reach measure is not a denominator of unique completed clinical courses. The [education page](https://www.sycamores.org/education-based-services/) separately reports over 1,175 students in 2024–25 and 81% with improved symptoms; neither establishes incremental improvement versus alternative care.

A [practice implementation study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37091107/) compares routine modular-therapy outcomes with research benchmarks. It supports feasibility but is not a new randomized donation experiment. The next useful evidence is unique clinical offers, diagnosis and age eligibility, course intensity, CHU9D or equivalent follow-up, payer replacement and residence. Deduplicate clients moving among school, clinic, housing and crisis services.
sections.qualitative:
The [California Child STEPs trial](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27548030/), with Hathaway-Sycamores investigators, randomized community therapists treating 138 children to modular MATCH therapy or county-supported evidence-based alternatives. Caregiver-reported improvement was 60% versus 36.7%, with faster clinical and functional improvement under MATCH. This is unusually relevant evidence of treatment quality, but it is not a 23.3-percentage-point effect of every ordinary donation today: alternative providers may now use similar methods.

The [MICE economic trial](https://doi.org/10.1192/bjo.2025.10916) supplies a separate health bridge: Table 3 reports about 0.022 additional child QALY over 12 months for a modified modular intervention. It studied 334 UK children with epilepsy and mental-health disorders; utility measurement was almost entirely caregiver-proxy report and economic data were incomplete. Transfer to Sycamores is a substantial judgment. The model halves the effect, limits it to compatible offers and adds no lifetime extrapolation or second clinical-response multiplier.

The numerical illustration covers the large community/clinic service line, which represents about 59% of gross recipient expense. Residential, housing and crisis pathways could add important health value, or create harms and substitution. Their omission is not evidence of zero value and prevents interpreting this as a whole-portfolio return.
sections.cost:
The retained partial clinical reference is $140,881,308.91 per ten LA clinical QALYs at $69,182,014 full annual recipient resources. Signed household resources remain assessed and unknown, not zero, a complete portfolio valuation or an empirical 90% health finding.

The current [housing page](https://www.sycamores.org/homeless-housing-support/) reports 167 transition-age youth housed between 2024 and 2025, not 167 new annual financial households. The no-rent program and furnished housing supply real consumption, but market rent cannot automatically become displaced private cash. Actual residence duration, alternative foster/public housing, food costs, benefits retained and net work resources remain unresolved. Workforce training participation is not a wage or placement effect. Existing LAHSA/Pasadena hotel-voucher financing belongs in the counterfactual.

The [Family Resource Center](https://www.sycamores.org/family-resource-center/) offers free food, tutoring and financial-aid application support, without actual retained awards or displaced spending per household. [Behavioral health](https://www.sycamores.org/behavioral-health/) involves family participation and possible telehealth; fees, travel, childcare, caregiver time and work losses must be netted jointly against existing care and alternative arrangements. Full incurred costs survive clinical nulls and are never reduced by symptom success. Positive health/housing overlap limits gains only. Public/provider savings, retail care/housing value and gross future wages are not disposable family income.

A conditional numerical resource bridge does not require an RCT, but a matched amount/duration and unique household incidence are still needed. The original seven clinical worlds and full frozen diagnostic remain valid partial references; the income-unknown case leaves combined welfare unpriced.

FY2025 gross recipient expense is $69,182,014: Form 990 Part IX $69,100,380 plus $81,634 direct event costs netted against revenue. Corresponding FY2024 and FY2023 totals are $67,014,960 and $63,268,616. The three-year mean is $66,488,530. No rental, gaming or inventory addback was shown. [2025 return](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202631249349302098/IRS990) [2024](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202531329349304133/IRS990) [2023](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202411369349302771/IRS990)

Schedule D records no donated-service expense exclusion in these years. For FY2025, $69,078,551 audited-statement expense plus $21,829 investment expenses reconciles to Part IX before restoring event costs. Recognized donated goods are not added twice. This is gross accrual recipient cost, not cash spending or a consolidated audit valuation of every volunteer hour. [Filed reconciliation](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202631249349302098/IRS990ScheduleD)

The conditional clinical model yields 4.91 LA QALYs at full recipient cost, or approximately $140.88 million per 10. Joint positive stress cases range from $3.37 million to $249.06 billion, not confidence limits. The financial denominator is observed; the assumed $10,000 per compatible clinical offer and other transfer/funding parameters are not observed unit costs. A whole-portfolio price remains unknown.

For the entire recipient to achieve $1 million per 10 LA QALYs requires 691.82014 annual net LA QALYs; $100,000 requires 6,918.2014. Outside medical care, housing resources not recorded here and family time remain additional social costs, not deductions from the donation denominator.
sections.funding:
FY2025 government grants were $67,934,754, against total revenue of $74,686,044. Net assets were $18,899,456, including $14,037,548 without donor restrictions; cash and savings together were $1,843,950. These amounts do not identify a currently unfilled unrestricted service gap. [Original return](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202631249349302098/IRS990)

The [state's May 2025 announcement](https://www.dhcs.ca.gov/news/california-to-expand-behavioral-health-care-in-los-angeles-county/) describes funded crisis-facility development in Altadena. Planned slots are not verified delivered outcomes, and existing capital commitments belong in the baseline. The education service page also identifies CYBHI public funding. New gifts may fund uncovered care or improve implementation, but may also substitute for contracts, reserves or other donors.

The 25% funding responsiveness assumption means that a proportional recipient funding increment changes one-quarter of corresponding clinical capacity. It is a judgment, not a claim that 25% of current clients would otherwise receive no help. An uncovered staffing proposal, caseload evidence and public-contract renewal terms could materially revise it. No outreach or gift was made.

model.costScope: Full recipient resources; priced health is a dominant-clinical component, not entire portfolio.
model.geographicAttribution: g=.9 is a clinical residence prior excluding Riverside; not an observed share and not applied to nationwide training.
model.formula: Q_component=(D*e/u)*q*t*b*g/(1+d). D=40872560,e=.5,u=10000,q=.022,t=.5,b=.25,g=.9,d=.03 gives Q=4.91065951456; Price10=10*69182014/Q. Q_portfolio=Q_component+Q_other-H; unpriced Q_other remains unknown.
model.counterfactual: County-supported alternative therapy and existing capacity continue; funding responsiveness concerns extra recipient resources, not the absence of all services. MICE already compares with enhanced usual care.
model.attribution: Use clinical offers once, not all 37000 people reached or every crisis encounter. No multiplication by the separate MATCH improvement rate, session count or completion probability. Caregiver effects appear only in a separately labeled sensitivity.
model.uncertainty: Conditional component best estimate with subjective delivery and transfer priors; not a complete portfolio estimate or statistical interval. Zero and adverse outcomes are possible.
model.nativeOutcomes: D*e/u=2043.628 compatible offer-equivalents; after transfer and funding, 255.4535 reference-effect-equivalent offers; geography and timing yield 4.91066 LA QALYs. Counts are modeled expectations, not observed marginal patients.

inputs.name: D
inputs.rationale: Largest Part III service line; used only to model delivery, not the cost denominator.

inputs.name: e
inputs.rationale: Half of the service line is assumed suitable for a modular youth-treatment offer; test .2–.8.

inputs.name: u
inputs.unit: USD clinical service-line resources per compatible offer
inputs.rationale: Conservative planning prior, not an observed unit cost; test 5000–20000. Includes clinical direct and support activity within D.

inputs.name: q
inputs.unit: additional child QALY per randomized offer over 12 months
inputs.rationale: Rounded MICE Table 3 child estimate, not combined caregiver QALYs or per completed session.

inputs.name: t
inputs.rationale: Different clinical population and modern alternative care; test .1–1.

inputs.name: b
inputs.rationale: Capacity change after public and donor substitution; test .05–.75.

inputs.name: g
inputs.unit: LA/Orange resident share of clinical component
inputs.rationale: Riverside excluded; residence distribution not observed. Test .7–.98.

inputs.name: d
inputs.rationale: Discounts future annual offer once; q already includes a finite 12-month trajectory.

inputs.name: Q_other
inputs.rationale: Residential, housing, crisis and training pathways remain unpriced.

incomeAssessment.scope: Targeted transition-age housing, food, aid, private payments and family attendance/work costs; original clinical reference retained.
incomeAssessment.rationale: Housing and food programs supply concrete service cohorts/mechanisms, but no matched private-payment displacement, retained benefit amount, duration or net earnings. Zero-rent participation and training do not establish household disposable gains at market prices.
directions: No-rent housing can replace actual rent or alternative free foster/public housing; rent, food and aid must be jointly compared over finite residence.
Food support and financial-aid applications require actual displaced spending/retained awards, not retail basket value or applications as cash.
Private treatment payments, transport, childcare, caregiver time and work losses apply independently of clinical response; positive overlap only limits gains.
Existing LAHSA/Pasadena, county care and other providers remain baseline; public savings/provider budgets and gross future wages are not client income.

priceScope: Conditional clinical-component estimate charging full recipient expenses; other program effects are not estimated
